title: You thought it was the enemy.
paragraphs:
You thought it was the enemy.
That sudden “no.”
That opportunity that collapsed right when you were sure it was God.
That relationship that ended without warning.
That door… slammed shut.
And you whispered it under your breath—
“The devil is blocking me.”
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Not every closed door is the devil.
Some of them are God’s mercy.
You were ready to walk through it.
You prayed about it—kind of.
You felt peace—at least, you convinced yourself you did.
You even told people, “I think this is from God.”
But deep down…
You knew something was off.
God saw it.
You knew.
That quiet hesitation.
That small conviction you kept overriding.
That Scripture you skimmed past because it didn’t match what you wanted.
You didn’t want discernment.
You wanted permission.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
There’s a moment in Scripture that doesn’t get talked about enough.
In the book of Revelation, Jesus says:
“I know your works. See, I have set before you an open door, and no one can shut it…” (Revelation 3:8)
Read that again.
If God opens a door,
no one can shut it.
Not demons.
Not people.
Not delays.
Not confusion.
So if it closed…
who really closed it?
You don’t like that question.
Because it shifts everything.
It means maybe—
just maybe—
you weren’t being attacked.
You were being redirected.
Or even more uncomfortable…
you were being stopped.
“For the Lord God is a sun and shield; the Lord bestows favor and honor. No good thing does He withhold from those who walk uprightly.” (Psalm 84:11)
No good thing.
So if it was withheld…
was it really good?
Or was it just something you desired more than God?
Let’s be honest.
You’ve called things “spiritual warfare” that were actually consequences.
You’ve rebuked the devil for doors God Himself shut.
You’ve labeled correction as opposition.
And all the while…
God was protecting you from something you couldn’t see.
That job?
It would have consumed you and pulled you further from Him.
That relationship?
It would have slowly normalized sin until conviction felt like noise.
That opportunity?
It would have elevated your platform—but buried your soul.
But you couldn’t see that.
Because desire can feel like destiny when you’re not anchored in truth.
“There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way to death.” (Proverbs 14:12)
Seems right.
Feels right.
Looks right.
But leads to death.
And God, in His mercy,
will shut a door to keep you from walking into destruction.
Even if it hurts.
Even if it confuses you.
Even if it makes you question everything.
That “no” wasn’t rejection.
It was protection.
But here’s where it gets deeper…
Sometimes God closes doors not just to protect you from something—
but to expose something in you.
Your impatience.
Your pride.
Your need for control.
Your addiction to outcomes.
Because when the door closed,
you didn’t run to God.
You got frustrated.
You questioned Him.
You started forcing other doors.
You revealed what you trust most.
“Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding.” (Proverbs 3:5)
Lean not.
But you did.
You leaned into your plans.
Your timelines.
Your expectations.
And when God interrupted it…
you called it warfare.
But it was actually invitation.
An invitation to trust Him beyond what you can see.
An invitation to surrender what you think you need.
An invitation to stop chasing open doors—
and start following the One who opens them.
Because the truth is…
You don’t need every door to open.
You just need the right one.
And the right one will never require you to compromise your obedience.
It won’t pull you away from Christ.
It won’t silence conviction.
It won’t demand that you ignore Scripture.
God doesn’t contradict Himself to give you what you want.
So if the door requires you to step outside His Word…
it didn’t come from Him.
No matter how good it looks.
No matter how badly you want it.
Now the tension hits.
Because you’re thinking about that one thing.
That door you’re still trying to reopen.
That situation you keep revisiting.
That person you’re still holding onto.
That path you refuse to release.
You’re asking God to open it again.
And He’s been silent.
Not because He’s absent.
But because He already answered.
No.
And you’re still negotiating.
But grace doesn’t mean God will bless your disobedience.
Grace means He will keep calling you back.
“For those whom the Lord loves He disciplines…” (Hebrews 12:6)
That closed door?
That might be discipline.
Not punishment.
Correction.
Realignment.
Love that refuses to let you drift into destruction.
So now you’re standing in front of it.
Still.
Waiting.
Conflicted.
You can keep knocking…
or you can finally trust the One who closed it.
Because on the other side of surrender—
there’s a door you didn’t expect.
One you didn’t manipulate.
One you didn’t force.
One that aligns with His will, not just your desire.
And when that one opens…
you won’t have to strive.
You’ll know.
Peace won’t be something you manufacture.
It will be something God establishes.
Say it plainly—“God, I release what You closed.”
Not for performance.
Not for appearance.
But because you know He’s been dealing with you.
If you’ve been blaming the devil for something God shut down,
it’s time to realign.
Follow this path if you’re ready to stop chasing doors
and start walking with Christ in truth, correction, and real transformation.
There’s deeper teaching, sharper conviction, and real spiritual growth waiting.
If you’re serious about going deeper, about understanding God’s voice, His discipline, His will—step into it:

Because not every closed door is loss.
Some of them are the very thing that kept your soul alive.
